clue.text: Acknowledgment hard bread must be sent back

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the bread's letters are read from the end

parts.note: pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread

explanation.surface: A complaint at a restaurant: the waiter acknowledges that the stale bread has to go back to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be sent back' reverses only the bread, not the H; pitta is a Middle Eastern flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat tip is a small gesture of credit or recognition, the courtesy of touching one's hat.

clue.text: Assistant keeps son out of the way

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an aide is an assistant or helper
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A helper looks after someone's boy, keeping him clear of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set aside is moved off to one side, apart from the main business.

clue.text: Examiner buttons lip for a term

indicators.note: buttoning something up encloses it, so the examiner wraps round the lip

parts.note: a tester is one who examines or checks
a rim is a lip or edge, as of a cup

explanation.surface: An examiner keeps quiet, buttoning his lip for a whole term.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a period of three months, used in some academic calendars as a term.

clue.text: Homer perhaps with good information about Odysseus's origin

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good or sanctimonious in crosswords

indicators.note: about means around, so the information surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: a word's origin is where it begins, its opening letter

explanation.surface: The poet Homer, with sound information about how Odysseus began his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the Greek poet, given Odysseus; a homer is a homing pigeon. 'about' puts O inside GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, bred to find its way back to its loft; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Rehearse chapter at start of Thessalonians during worship

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so these letters go inside the word for worship

parts.note: to praise God is to worship

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A preacher rehearses reading a chapter from the start of Thessalonians in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a piece is to rehearse it, going over it repeatedly to improve.

clue.text: After exercise, painful, take top off lotion for such lovely skin

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
after exercise one aches; a body that aches is painful

indicators.note: the top of a word written down is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: hand cream is a lotion for the skin

explanation.surface: Aching after a workout, you skip the hand cream yet still have a lovely complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take top off' drops the H of HANDCREAM, leaving ANDCREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A peaches-and-cream complexion is fair and rosy, an idiom for flawless, healthy-looking skin.

clue.text: Sharpness was effective cutting very fine line

parts.note: ace means excellent, very fine

indicators.note: cutting into something means entering it, so the word for was effective goes inside the line

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
a measure that bit took hold and had an effect

explanation.surface: A sharp pencil worked well at drawing a very fine line.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbity is harshness or sharpness of tone or taste, a bitter edge.

clue.text: A pastoral letter: some felt it useful

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A churchgoer remarks that a few listeners found the bishop's pastoral letter helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to Titus is one of the Pastoral Epistles of the New Testament, a letter of guidance to a church leader.

clue.text: One chirping adds some weight to conversation

parts.note: a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds
a chat is an informal conversation

explanation.surface: A chatterbox adds gravity to the talk, chirping away.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small songbird whose call sounds like two stones knocked together.

clue.text: Vicar's adequate stipend?

parts.note: a vicar's post is called a living, so his pay would whimsically be his living's wage; the phrase means pay enough to live on

explanation.surface: A question about whether a clergyman earns enough.
explanation.walkthrough: A living is a Church of England benefice, the post and income of a parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A living wage is pay high enough to cover basic costs, which is what an adequate stipend is.

clue.text: Times has often run leaders as "The Thunderer"

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the next words, and a nod to newspaper leading articles

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper, nicknamed The Thunderer, has often run editorials in that vein.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times was nicknamed The Thunderer in the 19th century, so the surface reads as newspaper history.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, wielder of the hammer Mjolnir.

clue.text: Giant man comes in to pour tea without hesitation

indicators.note: the man enters the phrase, so his letters go inside it
without means lacking, so the hesitation is dropped

parts.note: to be mother is the British idiom for pouring the tea
er is a hesitant sound
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: A huge man arrives to serve tea, doing so without faltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be mother' is British for pouring the tea; 'without' drops the hesitation from its end, and 'comes in' puts the man inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is a huge biblical beast, so the word names anything enormous, a giant.

clue.text: Stand for body keeping our people in additional employment

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the stand surrounds our people

parts.note: a bier is the stand on which a coffin or corpse rests
us means our people, we ourselves

explanation.surface: Undertakers' talk: a coffin stand keeps their staff even more occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is comparative: someone in additional employment is more occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: Busier means more fully occupied with work, having extra tasks on hand.

clue.text: Half of capital being lost is a nuisance

indicators.note: half of a word is taken, here its second half since the first half, BUDA, is lost

parts.note: Budapest is the capital of Hungary

explanation.surface: Losing half your money is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being lost' says the other half, Buda, is gone; Budapest was formed from Buda and Pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or thing, a nuisance.

clue.text: Building work noise dealt with next

indicators.note: letters dealt out like cards are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Next, the neighbours complain about the noise from the building work.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an addition built onto a house, a common building project.

clue.text: Don't budge, being too drunk to stand up?

definitions.meaning: to stay where you are and not move

definitions.text: being too drunk to stand up?
definitions.meaning: whimsically, sitting because one is tight, drunk

explanation.surface: Advice to a reveller who has had far too much to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit tight is an idiom for staying put; tight is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Just over three foot channels, note, are direct

parts.note: a metre is just over three feet, written 1M, read as IM
media are channels of communication
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A water engineer's spec: channels slightly over a yard wide run straight.
explanation.walkthrough: One metre is about 3 feet 3 inches; '1M' looks like the letters IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means with nothing in between, so direct, as in an immediate cause.

clue.text: More white people in the leading position before

indicators.note: the leading position of a word is its first letter

parts.note: earlier means before in time

explanation.surface: Fairer-skinned people held the top positions before, a pointed historical remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearly means white and lustrous like a pearl, so pearlier is whiter.

clue.text: Got nurse cooking large fish

indicators.note: cooking turns ingredients into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse has started cooking a big fish for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, source of caviar.

clue.text: Modest offering from overseas university: English

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a university in the USA

explanation.surface: A small donation arrives from a foreign university's English department.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospels a poor widow gave two mites, a small but heartfelt gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a very small sum or contribution, from the widow's mite in the Bible.

clue.text: Electrician is avoiding risk in baths

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word for baths

parts.note: spas are places with mineral baths

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so the word risk loses the two letters of the word before

explanation.surface: An electrician steers clear of danger when working near bathtubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link verb, but it is the letters dropped from the risk, and 'avoiding' signals that loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is the traditional nickname for an electrician or radio operator.

clue.text: Nothing missing from a different part of plant

indicators.note: missing from means absent from, so the nothing is removed

parts.note: another means a different one
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is lacking from a different part of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a flower's stamen.

clue.text: God takes a long time turning over ancient city

indicators.note: turning over flips the city inside the word, so its two letters swap order

parts.note: hours means a long time, as in 'it took hours'
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A deity takes ages in overturning an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky god of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Boy quivered, intermittently showing filthy greed

parts.note: Cupid, the boy god of love, carries a quiver of arrows

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A boy trembles, now and then revealing a dirty, grasping nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupidity is avarice, a strong desire for wealth, so greed.

clue.text: Fountain: in it tossed up clergyman

indicators.note: in places the clergyman inside the reversed word
in a down entry, tossed up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman is thrown up into a fountain, coins and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed up' turns IT into TI. Tourists toss coins into the Trevi.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trevi Fountain in Rome is famed for visitors throwing coins into it.

clue.text: Sort of glass construction in the sea

definitions.meaning: a ... glass is a tall mirror hung between windows
a structure built out into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Pier names both a structure jutting into water and, in pier glass, the wall between windows.

clue.text: It gets people mixing cocktail ingredient right into tumbler

parts.note: ice goes into many cocktails

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking cup or tumbler

explanation.surface: A bartender's instruction: drop a cocktail ingredient straight into a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' looks like cocktails, but here means socialising.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is a game or remark that eases social awkwardness so strangers mingle.

clue.text: Physicist's unusually strong backing graduate receives

definitions.note: the possessive points to what belongs to the physicist, the unit bearing his name

indicators.note: receives means takes inside, so the graduate surrounds the jumble
backing means going backwards, so the graduate's letters are reversed

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: unusually signals the word strong arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A physicist with an unusually strong supporter who is a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns MA into AM, and 'unusually' rearranges STRONG into NGSTRO, which AM receives.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Ångström was a Swedish physicist whose name is given to a tiny unit of length.

clue.text: Reasonably decide to reverse charge, one set in stone

indicators.note: set in means placed inside, so these letters go within the stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

indicators.note: to reverse means to turn backwards, so the charge is read from the end

parts.note: a fee is a charge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A judge might decide to reverse a charge, carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' acts on the charge alone; a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To see fit is to judge something proper or suitable, deciding as you think reasonable.
